answer.text: Quantitative models to identify short-term pricing anomalies; positions held briefly

explanation.text: The Logic: Statistical arbitrage ("Stat Arb") is a quantitative trading approach that uses statistical and mathematical models to identify short-term mispricings or anomalies between related securities. Positions are typically held for brief periods — minutes to days — and the strategy depends on a large number of small, near-uncorrelated bets where statistical edge plays out over many trades. Fundamental-analysis-only, long-term buy-and-hold, and macroeconomic-only approaches operate on entirely different time horizons and signal sets. The Trap: Fundamental-only and long-term buy-and-hold strategies sound rigorous but they are not Stat Arb — Stat Arb's defining features are the quantitative model and the short holding period. Note: The specific labels "Statistical arbitrage" or "Stat Arb" and the "short-term pricing anomalies / brief holding periods" framing are not used in the NISM Series XIX-B AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook pages checked (which discuss arbitrage, managed futures, market-neutral, global macro and long/short in general terms); the framing above reflects general hedge-fund industry terminology rather than a workbook citation.
